explanation: Passing electricity through concentrated brine splits it into sodium hydroxide, chlorine gas at the anode and hydrogen gas at the cathode — the industrial chlor-alkali process that supplies the raw materials for bleaching powder and several other everyday chemicals.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: A colourless brine solution, with two electrodes dipped in.
beaker_view.final_appearance: Still colourless; sodium hydroxide has formed near the cathode.
beaker_view.observation: Bubbles of gas rise steadily from each electrode as the current flows, while sodium hydroxide slowly forms in the solution.
